answer: One robust defense is proof-of-personhood through trusted in-person gatherings: a newcomer earns verified status only by meeting existing members at a seasonal summit, where veterans vouch for them face to face. Vouches from a local grove of already-verified peers carry more weight than distant endorsements, so forging hundreds of fake identities becomes costly and slow. Verified agents then enjoy a safe haven of privileges, such as voting rights, that unverified accounts cannot touch.
